newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee due sharply up, seen testing $2,190.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee due sharply up, seen testing $2,190.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures are called to open $140 higher on numbers on the back of another surge in New York on Tuesday but traders said in practice, the market could be content with $50-$75 up.
Technically, coffee remains bullish and benchmark July looks set to test and clear a key resistance at $2,190, the May 19 peak.
New York's arabica coffee futures exploded higher on Tuesday, with the benchmark July contract surging nearly seven percent, as continued supply concerns fuelled a speculative-led rally.
The contract shot up to a new life-of-contract high of 275.00 cents per lb before settling at 274.30 cents, up a hefty 17.45 cents on the day.
"The perception is that supply is tight and will remain tight into the December contract," said Refco analyst Ann Prendergast.
London's robustas were dragged up higher on Tuesday afternoon by surging New York values, with July finishing the day above the closely-watched $2,100 a tonne level.
Chart-wise, the contract could still go much higher, said Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden.
A break above the immediate $2,190 hurdle could pave the way to the next upside goal at $2,319, a 38.1 percent retracement from the bear phase in 1994, he said.
"Look likes the market is trading out of the flag (continuation) pattern," he said. The bottom of the of the range is $2,030 and the top is $2,190.
Below that, there is a chart gap at between $1,940 and $1,973. "While the gap remains open, I am going to remain bullish of the market."
The 10-day moving average is bullish at 2,021.
But the market is well over-bought with the nine-day relative strength indicator standing at 85 percent, well above the 70-value barrier.
The market's main concern is the Brazilian weather as the country's coffee belt enters the dangerous frost months in June and July.
U.S. private forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday somewhat cooler than normal conditions were expected in the coffee belt this week.
But no damaging cold is indicated and there are no cold air masses expected to build out of Argentina during the next five to seven days. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
